facts.text: OmnirobotEnv-v0 is registered to the OmniRobotEnv class
The registry builds the entry point from env_class.__module__ + ':' + env_class.__name__
USING_OMNIROBOT_SIMULATOR defaults to True

When USING_OMNIROBOT_SIMULATOR is true the environment constructs OmniRobotSimulatorSocket with output_size [RENDER_WIDTH, RENDER_HEIGHT] and random_target; otherwise it connects a ZMQ PAIR socket to HOSTNAME:self.server_port
The separate ROS server creates publishers for /position_commands, /stop, /wheel_speeds_commands and /velocity_commands
The separate ROS server publishes True to both position and velocity controller switches during construction
is_discrete defaults to True
The default action space is spaces.Discrete(N_DISCRETE_ACTIONS)
N_DISCRETE_ACTIONS is 4
The discrete action values are FORWARD 0, BACKWARD 1, LEFT 2, RIGHT 3 and STOP 4
A step sends the action to the simulator socket, reads the state, receives and resizes the camera frame, and returns a 4-tuple (observation, reward, done, {})
A reset clears the episode flag and the step and contact counters, sends the reset command, reads the state and observation, and returns the observation without an info dictionary
The native reset signature takes no arguments besides self
RENDER_WIDTH and RENDER_HEIGHT are 224
The observation space is Box(0, 255, shape=(RENDER_WIDTH, RENDER_HEIGHT, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
The simulator samples the robot's initial x and y with numpy's random_sample from the INIT_MIN/MAX bounds
INIT_MIN_X = -0.7, INIT_MAX_X = 0.7, INIT_MIN_Y = -0.7 and INIT_MAX_Y = 0.7
On a reset the simulator draws a target in x and y with numpy's random_sample from the TARGET_MIN/MAX bounds when random_target is true or on the first episode
TARGET_MIN_X = -0.7, TARGET_MAX_X = 0.7, TARGET_MIN_Y = -0.7 and TARGET_MAX_Y = 0.7
MIN_X = -0.85, MAX_X = 0.85, MIN_Y = -0.85 and MAX_Y = 0.85
STEP_DISTANCE is 0.1 m
A forward move is refused when robot_pos[0] + STEP_DISTANCE is not below MAX_X and the manager reports a bump; backward, left and right use MIN_X, MAX_Y and MIN_Y analogously
The reward is REWARD_TARGET_REACH when the robot-target distance is below DIST_TO_TARGET_THRESHOLD, REWARD_BUMP_WALL for a wall bump and REWARD_NOTHING otherwise
REWARD_TARGET_REACH is 1, REWARD_NOTHING is 0 and REWARD_BUMP_WALL is -1
DIST_TO_TARGET_THRESHOLD is 0.2 m
MAX_STEPS is 250
_hasEpisodeTerminated returns True when episode_terminated is set or the step counter is greater than MAX_STEPS
SRLGymEnv.seed sets np_random and returns [seed]
The simulator samples positions with numpy's random_sample()

determinism.notes: the fake's legacy seed() controls the fake's own generator, so the fake repeats a trajectory for one seed and action sequence; upstream SRLGymEnv.seed sets np_random only and the simulator draws from numpy's global generator (environments/srl_env.py:71-78, real_robots/omnirobot_utils/omnirobot_manager_base.py:88-89), so the upstream simulator is not seeded by this path

fidelity.engine: gymnasium:OmnirobotEnv-v0 (analytic fake of the in-process simulator)
gaps: action.index 0..3 is derived from the declared fake's Discrete(4), with fake-backend provenance; there is no action_space_ref claiming that the symbolic native space declaration by itself shows the maximum index. Native Discrete(N_DISCRETE_ACTIONS), N_DISCRETE_ACTIONS=4 and movement codes 0..3 are cited separately in the facts

the fake is an analytic stand-in for the discrete simulator, not a recording: it models the 0.1 m moves, the 0.85 wall bumps, the 0.2 m target reward and the 251-step termination from real_robots/omnirobot_utils/omnirobot_manager_base.py:22-158 and real_robots/constants.py:78-121

no rendering: the background image, marker sprites, camera projection, 480 x 480 crop and 224 x 224 resize are not modelled; the fake returns a 16 x 16 x 3 placeholder marker image while the device returns a 224 x 224 x 3 image (environments/omnirobot_gym/omnirobot_env.py:29-30,120-122,229-239)
no noise: the robot position (0.01 m), yaw, marker size and image luminosity noise of real_robots/omnirobot_simulator_server.py:16-22 are not modelled, and positions are exact
the fake's seed() controls its own generator; the upstream simulator's random draws use numpy's global generator and are not controlled by SRLGymEnv.np_random
the Gymnasium family advertises reset options, but the native reset takes no arguments; the bridge's legacy fallback calls seed() and reset() without them, so an options value is not used
one step is one discrete command of 0.1 m, not a physics integration interval: no physics timestep is declared, hence timestep_ms 0 and no wall-clock pacing
the PyBullet, Gazebo and ROS paths are not modelled; the fake runs in the package and the upstream simulator or ROS bridge was not run

the non-simulator ZMQ route can reach the separate real-robot ROS server, whose construction enables both position and velocity controllers (real_robots/omnirobot_server.py:71-92); the R0 contract and the software latch cover only the declared fake and the default in-process simulator, not that route
the fake was not compared with the upstream simulator; shape_reward is stored but unused, as in the clone, and the image is a placeholder rather than a camera frame

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
